sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: OVERALL PATTERN REMAINS SIMILAR TO SUNDAY WITH BROAD MID/UPPER LEVEL TROUGH PERSISTING FROM THE NRN PLAINS INTO THE CENTRAL ROCKIES...WHILE A SERIES OF LOWER AMPLITUDE TROUGHS ROTATE ENEWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL U.S. THROUGH THE PERIOD. THE SURFACE PATTERN HAS BECOME QUITE MUDDLED EARLY THIS MORNING ACROSS MUCH OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS INTO THE MID MS RIVER VALLEY/WRN GREAT LAKES FROM PRIOR DEEP MOIST CONVECTION...INCLUDING PERSISTENT MCS EVOLVING OVER A LARGE PART OF NERN/CENTRAL KS AT DAYBREAK. HOWEVER...PRIMARY SURFACE BAROCLINIC ZONE WILL LIKELY EXTEND WSWWD FROM THE CENTRAL GREAT LAKES INTO THE MID MS RIVER VALLEY AND THE NRN TX PANHANDLE TODAY. NRN/ERN HALF OF THIS BOUNDARY WILL LIKELY STRUGGLE TO DESTABILIZE WITH ONGOING CLOUDS/PRECIPITATION LIMITING HEATING AND GENERALLY WEAK MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES IN PLACE EAST OF THE PLAINS STATES. HOWEVER...AS WAS THE CASE YESTERDAY...MODEST SWLY FLOW ALOFT SHOULD PROVE SUFFICIENT FOR ORGANIZATION OF STRONGER STORMS TODAY WHERE POCKETS OF MODEST INSTABILITY CAN EVOLVE WITHIN BROADER AREA OF RELATIVELY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER. ISOLATED WIND DAMAGE IS LIKELY FROM PORTIONS OF THE LOWER MO/MID MS RIVER VALLEY NEWD INTO THE GREAT LAKES...ALTHOUGH COVERA

sections.title: FAR ERN MS/AL
sections.text: REMNANTS OF T.S. CLAUDETTE NOW OVER SERN AL WILL CONTINUE TO WEAKEN AS IT LIFTS NNWWD THROUGH THE DAY. AS LONG AS A LOW LEVEL CYCLONE REMAINS EVIDENT...RESULTANT INCREASE IN SFC-H85 WINDS WILL SUSTAIN AT LEAST A RISK OF A BRIEF TORNADO WITH ANY PERSISTENT UPDRAFT TODAY. AT THIS TIME...OVERALL THREAT REMAINS QUITE WEAK. ..EVANS/JEWELL.. 08/17/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: THE LARGE SCALE PATTERN WILL CHANGE LITTLE THROUGH TONIGHT AS A CLOSED LOW MOVES SLOWLY EWD FROM MANITOBA INTO WRN ONTARIO...AND A TRAILING TROUGH AXIS AND EMBEDDED SPEED MAXIMA PROGRESS EWD FROM THE NRN GREAT BASIN TOWARD THE CENTRAL ROCKIES. AT THE SURFACE...A SLOW-MOVING BAROCLINIC ZONE WILL EXTEND FROM UPPER MI/WI SWWD ACROSS IA AND KS TO NW OK AND THE TX PANHANDLE. THIS BOUNDARY...AND OTHER REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES FROM OVERNIGHT CONVECTION...WILL FOCUS THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE PERIOD FROM THE SRN/CENTRAL PLAINS INTO THE MIDWEST. ELSEWHERE...SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS CAN BE EXPECTED THROUGH THE DAY FROM E TX TO THE CAROLINAS. THE MORE CONCENTRATED THUNDERSTORMS WILL OCCUR ALONG THE I-10 CORRIDOR FROM LA EWD INTO SRN AL/FL PANHANDLE WITH THE REMNANT MOISTURE PLUME FROM WHAT WAS TROPICAL STORM CLAUDETTE. MORE ISOLATED STORMS WILL OCCUR THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS THE SRN APPALACHIANS AREA INTO CENTRAL NC ALONG THE SRN/SWRN FRINGE OF A WEAK MID LEVEL TROUGH DRIFTING EWD OVER NC/VA.

sections.title: MO/KS/OK/CO AREA THIS AFTERNOON THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: ONGOING CONVECTION ACROSS SRN KS WILL LIKELY PERSIST AND CONTINUE TO DEVELOP ALONG AND IMMEDIATELY N OF THE ASSOCIATED OUTFLOW-REINFORCED SURFACE FRONT THAT IS MOVING SEWD ACROSS SW MO/SE KS AND NW OK AS THE BOUNDARY LAYER WARMS/DESTABILIZES THROUGH THE AFTERNOON. THE CONVECTION ALONG THIS BOUNDARY WILL BE NEAR THE SERN FRINGE OF THE STRONGER MID LEVEL FLOW...THUS THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREATS WILL BE LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WITH MULTICELL CLUSTERS AND EMBEDDED BOWING SEGMENTS. FARTHER NW...MORE ELEVATED CONVECTION IS ALSO ONGOING FROM THE NE TX PANHANDLE INTO SW/CENTRAL KS IN ASSOCIATION WITH LOW-LEVEL WAA AND FRONTOGENESIS. THE 13Z DDC SOUNDING REVEALED SUFFICIENT INSTABILITY /MUCAPE IN EXCESS OF 2500 J/KG BASED NEAR 800 MB/ FOR LARGE HAIL WITH THE MORE INTENSE STORMS...AND POSSIBLY A DAMAGING WIND THREAT WITH DOWNDRAFTS OF MID LEVEL ORIGIN PENETRATING THE LOW-LEVEL STABLE LAYER N OF THE BOUNDARY. ADDITIONAL SEVERE STORMS MAY FORM LATER THIS AFTERNOON ACROSS SE CO IN THE UPSLOPE FLOW REGIME. SOME OF THIS CONVECTION MAY PERSIST AND SPREAD EWD/ESEWD OVERNIGHT INTO SW KS/NW OK AS AN MCS...AIDED BY THE SLY LLJ WHICH WILL STRENGTHEN AND FOCUS LOW-LEVEL WAA N OF THE COMPOSITE OUTFLO

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS PORTIONS CENTRAL/SRN PLAINS
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS PORTIONS MID MS RIVER VALLEY REGION... --- UPDATES ---

sections.title: CENTRAL/SRN PLAINS
sections.text: SFC MESOANALYSIS AND REFLECTIVITY ANIMATIONS EACH INDICATE WELL-DEFINED OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM OVERNIGHT THROUGH EARLY-AFTERNOON CONVECTION...EXTENDING SWWD FROM AFOREMENTIONED OZARKS ACTIVITY ACROSS EXTREME E-CENTRAL OK...THEN ROUGHLY ALONG I-40 WWD THROUGH OKC AREA...THEN WNWWD TOWARD GAG. SEGMENT OF BOUNDARY FROM NEAR SNL-OKC-GAG HAS BECOME QUASISTATIONARY...AND REMAINDER ERN OK SEGMENT OF BOUNDARY SHOULD DO LIKEWISE DURING NEXT COUPLE HOURS. SFC-BASED EVOLUTION/DEVELOPMENT OF CONVECTION IS ANTICIPATED DURING REMAINDER AFTERNOON S OF BOUNDARY AND WITHIN 50-75 NM TO ITS N. MOST FAVORABLE JUXTAPOSITION OF ENLARGED LOW LEVEL HODOGRAPH SIZE...LOW LEVEL MOIST AXIS...DEEP-LAYER SHEAR...AND LARGE LAPSE RATES/BUOYANCY IN SUPPORT OF AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING SUPERCELLS SHOULD BE IN CORRIDOR VERY NEAR BOUNDARY OVER PANHANDLES AND NW OK. UPSCALE EVOLUTION TO OVERNIGHT MCS STILL APPEARS POSSIBLE ACROSS PORTIONS KS/OK BORDER REGION. BEYOND THAT...ACROSS MOST OF CENTRAL/ERN KS...FCST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST EFFECTIVE INFLOW PARCELS WILL REMAIN ELEVATED ATOP RELATIVELY DEEP/STABLE OUTFLOW POOL.

sections.title: MID MS VALLEY REGION
sections.text: SOMEWHAT ORGANIZED BANDS OF SCATTERED-NUMEROUS TSTMS SHOULD CONTINUE TO MOVE GENERALLY EWD ACROSS REGION WITH PRIMARY CONCERN BEING DAMAGING GUSTS...AND ISOLATED HAIL ALSO POSSIBLE. REF SPC MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 1904 FOR MORE DETAILED NEAR-TERM FCST INFORMATION. THREAT SHOULD SUBSIDE THIS EVENING ONCE GRADUAL DIABATIC COOLING OF VERY MOIST INFLOW-LAYER AIR MASS DIMINISHES AVAILABLE BUOYANCY...AND ACTIVITY MOVES INTO REGIME OF WEAKER MID-UPPER LAPSE RATES. ..EDWARDS/COOK.. 08/17/2009 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1129 AM CDT MON AUG 17 2009/

sections.title: SERN CO/OK-TX PANHANDLE EWD THROUGH OK/SRN KS
sections.text: EARLY EVENING SURFACE ANALYSIS SHOWED A SYNOPTIC FRONT EXTENDING FROM SERN KS SWWD THROUGH WRN OK TO NW TX...WITH TWO OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES FROM EARLIER CONVECTION EXTENDING FROM WEST CENTRAL TO ERN OK. A VERY MOIST AIR MASS EXTENDING FROM THE TX/OK PANHANDLES EWD THROUGH OK/SRN KS BENEATH PLUME OF STEEP LAPSE RATES EXTENDING INTO CENTRAL KS/WRN OK WILL MAINTAIN A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS THROUGH THE OVERNIGHT PERIOD. INCREASING LOW LEVEL WAA REGIME ALONG NOSE OF STRENGTHENING LLJ EXTENDING INTO TX PANHANDLE/WRN OK TO SOUTH CENTRAL/SWRN KS WILL SUPPORT UPSCALE GROWTH INTO AT LEAST ONE MCS ACROSS THIS REGION THROUGH 12Z TUESDAY. THE DEGREE OF AVAILABLE INSTABILITY AND EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR /40-50 KT/ SUGGESTS ADDITIONAL ORGANIZED STORMS/SUPERCELLS WILL BE LIKELY WITH A THREAT FOR VERY LARGE HAIL...STRONG WIND GUSTS AND PERHAPS A TORNADO.

sections.title: NERN-EAST CENTRAL CO
sections.text: WATER VAPOR IMAGERY INDICATED A SHORTWAVE TROUGH ROUNDING A LONGWAVE TROUGH OVER THE GREAT BASIN...WITH THIS MID LEVEL FEATURE EXPECTED TO TRACK EWD FROM UT TO THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS BY 12Z TUESDAY. FORCING FOR ASCENT WITH THIS FEATURE COMBINED WITH MOIST UPSLOPE FLOW INTO THE CO FRONT RANGE SUGGESTS ADDITIONAL STORMS WILL BE LIKELY THIS EVENING. MODERATE INSTABILITY AND STRONG EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR /AROUND 50 KT/ WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORMS/SUPERCELLS WITH LARGE HAIL...STRONG WIND GUSTS AND PERHAPS A TORNADO. TORNADO THREAT SHOULD BE CONFINED TO ANY STORM THAT CAN TRACK EWD ALONG A SURFACE BOUNDARY THAT EXTENDS FROM EL PASO TO CHEYENNE COUNTIES CO.

sections.title: OZARKS TO LOWER OH VALLEY/CENTRAL GREAT LAKES
sections.text: EARLY EVENING REGIONAL RADARS/SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWED A QUASI-LINEAR MCS MOVING EWD THROUGH THE OZARKS...MID MS/LOWER OH VALLEYS AND INTO LOWER MI. TSTMS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE ACROSS THE ERN EDGE OF THIS ELONGATED SYSTEM AIDED IN THE NORTH BY FORCING FOR ASCENT ATTENDANT TO A MID LEVEL SHORT WAVE TROUGH TRACKING FROM IL TOWARD SWRN ONTARIO. FURTHER SOUTH...STRONGER INSTABILITY MAY TEND TO AID THE LONGEVITY OF ACTIVITY OVER THE OZARKS TO SERN MO. WEAKENING TREND IN AVAILABLE CONVECTIVE INSTABILITY AND THE LACK OF STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR ALONG THE EXTENT OF THIS MCS WILL PRECLUDE THE OVERALL SEVERE WEATHER THREAT OVERNIGHT. ..PETERS.. 08/18/2009
